body:
> that will be remembered by the editor

Are you sure?

IMO this is not a bug. Monitors are registered during project execution. And when you stop debugging, they (or maybe even just UI side) just don't get cleaned up.

> > that will be remembered by the editor
> 
> Are you sure?
> 
> IMO this is not a bug. Monitors are registered during project execution. And when you stop debugging, they (or maybe even just UI side) just don't get cleaned up.

I did another test (v4.4) now, and indeed the custom monitors are wiped when you close the editor (but not when you just close the game). I assumed that they were cached intentionally, with an example use case (how I'm using them):
- Select monitors that you are interested in, custom and built-in alike
- Run the project and observe the values
- Close it, make changes, and run again, monitoring the same values without having to go in and select them again

I personally find this to be a recurring process when working with performance-related issues.

Either way: if the editor "caching" of custom monitors is considered a bug, then this issue is obsolete. However, if it's an intended feature (which I support), then I would expect custom and built-in monitors to have identical behavior in this context.

> monitoring the same values

I'm not sure if these are the same values for the editor. How does the editor know that you still have a specific user monitor after project re-run? They are created during code execution. And can be added, for example, by clicking a button:

```gdscript
func _on_button_pressed() -> void:
	Performance.add_custom_monitor("MyCategory/MyMonitor", monitor_value)
```
And before you pressed button, there is just no custom monitor at all.

So I think this issue should be moved to https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals for more discussion as a separate feature.

> > monitoring the same values
> 
> I'm not sure if these are the same values for the editor. How does the editor know that you still have a specific user monitor after project re-run? They are created during code execution. And can be added, for example, by clicking a button:
> 
> func _on_button_pressed() -> void:
> 	Performance.add_custom_monitor("MyCategory/MyMonitor", monitor_value)
> 
> And before you pressed button, there is just no custom monitor at all.
> 
> So I think this issue should be moved to https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals for more discussion as a separate feature.

I see. Without knowing the monitoring back-end code, my assumption would be that add_custom_monitor is a "register this monitor if it doesn't already exist". Either way, agree with your conclusion, and I'll think about it a bit more and maybe make a proposal. Moving away from a runtime-scope, which is what I understand is the current design, sounds like a major change, so I'll have to think a bit about whether it is justified.

Thanks a lot for the input!
